title: Issue-detection invoke must require USE on the body's gateway secret_id, not just UPDATE on the experiment
answers: Can a user with access to their own experiment run issue detection with someone else's AI Gateway key?
Why does POST issues/invoke return 403 when secret_id is passed even though I can update the experiment?
Another user's gateway secret is being decrypted into an issue detection job, how is that blocked?
How is secret_id authorized on the issues invoke route in basic-auth?
body:
Symptom: a basic-auth user with UPDATE on their own experiment could make issue detection decrypt and use another user's AI Gateway secret (provider API key) by sending that `secret_id`.
Root cause: mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:validate_can_update_experiment was the only validator on (INVOKE_ISSUE_DETECTION, "POST"), while the handler passes the caller's secret_id to _fetch_provider_credentials, which reads the plaintext key.
Fix pattern: mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:validate_can_invoke_issue_detection requires UPDATE on the experiment and, when the JSON body has a truthy secret_id, USE on that secret via _get_gateway_secret_permission(secret_id).can_use. Register it for INVOKE_ISSUE_DETECTION in BEFORE_REQUEST_VALIDATORS.
Constraints: an absent or empty secret_id passes after the experiment check, matching the handler's `if secret_id:` guard. Unknown secret ids resolve to no grant and return 403, so the route is not an existence oracle. READ on the secret is not enough. genai/evaluate and scorer invoke take no secret_id and keep validate_can_update_experiment. A camelCase or endpoint_name route is not covered by this check.
Applies: basic-auth POST /ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/issues/invoke; any new invoke route that forwards a caller-supplied secret_id.
applies: basic-auth (--app-name basic-auth) issue-detection invoke route and any invoke route that consumes a gateway secret.
says: Users can run issue detection using another member's saved gateway credentials without permission.
Running issue detection returns permission denied even though I can edit the experiment.
Prevent unauthorized users from running issue detection jobs with another team's gateway API keys.
Issue detection should require explicit permission to use the selected AI Gateway secret.
Block experiment editors from triggering issue detection with gateway secrets they do not own.
search: Under basic-auth on POST /ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/issues/invoke, validate_can_invoke_issue_detection enforces both UPDATE permission on the experiment and USE permission on any truthy secret_id via _get_gateway_secret_permission(secret_id).can_use. This prevents users with experiment update rights from decrypting another user's AI Gateway secret key during issue detection invocation. Empty or absent secret_id passes after the experiment check, while unknown secret IDs return 403 to prevent existence oracle leaks; READ permission alone is insufficient. This check applies to issue detection invoke in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py and tests/server/auth/test_auth.py, excluding genai/evaluate, scorer invoke, or camelCase and endpoint_name routes.
